body:
The round76 source investigation found a promising hectorite lithium-extraction study, but its complete primary evidence is not yet available in the inspected artifacts. No hectorite owner or quantitative mechanism claim has been added.

Primary candidate: Dong et al., *Multistep incongruent hectorite dissolution controls lithium release*, DOI [10.1016/j.apgeochem.2026.107047](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apgeochem.2026.107047). Official Crossref and publisher XML metadata resolve the title and DOI. The publisher marks it open access, but the inspected XML contains only coredata; it does not include the methods, results, figures, or supplements. The October 2026 issue date should not be substituted for an unverified publication day.

Acquisition evidence on 2026-10-14:

- ScienceDirect web access returned HTTP 403; the DOI route was unavailable through the web tool.
- The publisher PDF API request returned HTTP 406 with a restricted-Accept error.
- The Crossref-registered XML route returned HTTP 200 and 2,017 bytes of metadata only.
- Exact-title repository searches did not yield a complete original in the returned results; the browser fallback reported that no browser was available.
- Older comparison source: Van Rompaey et al. (2002), DOI [10.1016/S0169-1317(02)00086-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0169-1317(02)00086-8), remains limited to publisher excerpts. The complete illustrated paper was not inspected.

Acceptance work:

1. Acquire complete original articles, relevant supplements, tables and figures through a legitimate publisher or deposited route; retain provenance and checksums.
2. Resolve mineral nomenclature and the exact experimental specimen, including fluorine substitution, fractionation and impurity phases.
3. Review acid controls, mass balances, denominators and measured versus modelled quantities before adding an explicitly abiotic dissolution mechanism.
4. Keep any mixed-clay patent bioleaching evidence separate; it cannot establish pure-hectorite microbial behavior without its own full assessment.
5. Curate only supported claims, with canonical history, named validation and a separate scientific review.

Local assessment prepared for the next PR: `research/sources/round76-hectorite/20261014T163029Z.{json,md}`. Raw official metadata and access responses are retained outside Git in `/private/tmp/cmm-round76-hectorite-research`.
title: Acquire complete hectorite dissolution originals before mechanism curation
